analysis.title: Werner Enterprises Inc. (WERN) 3Q26 EPS Inline with Pre-Announcement; Remain Buy-Rated
key_insights: WERN adjusted 3Q26 operating EPS was $0.16, in line with the pre-announced 15-16 cent range, versus FactSet consensus $0.16 and GSe $0.15.

3Q EPS carried $0.18 of cumulative QoQ cost headwind: rapidly rising fuel prices, driver recruitment and retention investments (6 cents), and a late-quarter insurance reserve adjustment on past claims. Fuel and insurance together were 12 cents.

For 4Q, management expects fuel headwinds to largely abate and elevated insurance costs to be contained to 3Q. Driver recruiting investments continue at a measured pace to position the fleet for growth in 2027.
GS cut its 4Q26 EPS estimate to $0.25 from $0.30. The $0.30 was itself cut from $0.52 at the pre-announcement. FY26 EPS goes to $0.65 from $0.70, while FY27 ($2.20) and FY28 ($2.85) are unchanged.

One-way truckload revenue per truck per week rose about 34% YoY in 3Q (vs +28% in 2Q, +26% GSe). Revenue per mile was +10% YoY and miles per tractor +22% YoY (vs +13% GSe). Management said one-way truckload margins improved 800bps YoY and total TTS margins 220bps YoY.

Trucking EBIT was $24M (consensus $24M, GSe about $23M). Logistics EBIT was about $1M. Consolidated adjusted OR was 97.8%, in line with consensus and GSe of 97.7%. Adjusted trucking OR ex-fuel surcharge was 95.9% vs 96.3% consensus and 96.0% GSe.

One-way truckload contracts are expected to be up double digits YoY as a starting point in early bids for year-end and 2027, versus HSD-LDD% signed last quarter and about MSD in 1Q. 4Q26 one-way revenue per mile is guided +10-13% YoY, and GS now projects +11.5%.

Dedicated revenue per truck per week guide for 2026 was raised at the low end to +4-5% YoY from +3-5%. Combined trucking fleet growth is guided to 16-17% YoY (prior 16-18%), driven by the FirstFleet acquisition adding about 2.4k Dedicated trucks.
Net capex guide was lowered to $190M-$205M from $215M-$250M. The 2026 effective tax rate guide is 24.5%-25.5%.

GS stays Buy and expects truckload equities' usual seasonal strength into 4Q as spot rates typically re-accelerate through the November and December peak. It also expects improving contract rate negotiations into 2027 on tight driver supply.

The CASS freight index turned positive YoY for the first time in 42 months (+2% in August, +1.9% in September). Spot rates ex-fuel remain about 20-30% below the 2021 peak. GS sees truckload as early in its inflection, with more earnings torque than rails.

GS sees a potential multi-year elevated contract-resigning cycle, with firmer hold into 1H27. It cites tight supply from carrier exits and bankruptcies, English-proficiency enforcement for drivers, and non-renewal of non-domiciled CDLs. This could push truckload EPS above consensus.
Price target is $49 (unchanged), based on about 17x P/E on mid-cycle EPS of $2.90. Blue-sky mid-cycle EPS of $3.50 at 17x implies about $60 per share. Price is $29.38, implying 66.8% upside.

Adjusted TTS OR ex-fuel deteriorated about 140bps QoQ against a pre-Covid seasonal proxy of about 50bps, which GS reads as slightly sub-seasonal improvement. Logistics adjusted OR was 99.6% vs 101.3% in 2Q and 100.4% in 1Q.

market_movers.rationale: 3Q26 EPS was in line after the pre-announcement. GS sees seasonal 4Q strength, a tightening truckload market and a contract-rate reset into 2027. The price target is unchanged at $49.

sector_views.rationale: Early-stage market inflection with tight driver supply, improving contract rates into 2027 and more earnings torque than rails. GS upgraded truckers in June 2025 for early-cycle leverage.
GS moderated ratings on the more defensive cyclicals, rails and intermodal-adjacent names such as JBHT, in favor of trucking.

earnings_insights: WERN 3Q26 reported 10/27: adjusted recurring EPS $0.16 vs GSe $0.15 and FactSet consensus $0.16. This matched the pre-announced 15-16 cent range.
3Q26 revenue was $951M vs GSe $947M and consensus $957M. EBIT was $21.0M vs GSe $21.9M and consensus $22.3M. Recurring net income was $9.4M vs GSe $8.8M and consensus $8.3M.
3Q26 adjusted operating ratio was 97.8% vs 97.7% for both GSe and consensus. TTS OR was 96.6% and TTS OR ex-fuel 95.9% (GSe 96.0%). Werner Logistics OR was 99.6% (GSe 99.5%).
GS estimates: 4Q26 EPS $0.25 (from $0.30), FY26 EPS $0.65 (from $0.70), FY27 EPS $2.20 (unchanged), FY28 EPS $2.85 (unchanged). GS FY26 revenue is $3,646.4M, and EBITDA is $388.2M.
The FirstFleet acquisition is expected by management to be immediately accretive, with additional upside once $18M of synergies begin to materialize.

macro_indicators.reading: +1.9% YoY in September, +2% YoY in August
macro_indicators.interpretation: First positive YoY reading in 42 months, a sign trucking volumes are inflecting.

macro_indicators.indicator: Spot trucking rates ex-fuel vs 2021 peak
macro_indicators.interpretation: Spot rates are elevated YoY but have room to rise, supporting a view that the truckload cycle is early-stage.

trade_ideas.description: Buy WERN (Buy rating, $49 12-month price target) into seasonal 4Q truckload strength and 2027 contract-rate resets
trade_ideas.rationale: Seasonal spot-rate re-acceleration, tight driver supply and improving contract negotiations should lift truckload shares, with near-term cost pressure looked through.
trade_ideas.risk: Slower than expected volume growth, truck capacity influx or lack of capacity exiting, inability to push contract rates higher, inflationary cost pressures, insurance payout risk, recession with tariff risk, and quarterly fuel headwinds.

risk_factors: An influx of truck capacity, or lack of capacity exiting the market.
Inability to push contract rates higher.
Recession, many in conjunction with tariff-related risk.
Tight driver supply raises driver-related cost pressure, as seen in JBHT earnings and WERN's pre-announcement.

geopolitical: US administration focus on truck drivers' English proficiency and non-renewal of non-domiciled CDLs is tightening driver supply.
